records.jp: 君、なんだこの食べ物は。<CR>とろけるように甘くて、そしてひんやりとしているぞ
records.en_original: Explain this food to me. It's frigid, but it's still so smooth and sweet.
records.en_auxiliary: Explain this food to me. It's frigid, but it's still so smooth and sweet.
records.en: What is this food?<CR>It is sweet enough to melt in my mouth, yet pleasantly cold.

records.jp: パフェ、食べたことないの？
records.en_original: You've...never eaten a parfait before?
records.en_auxiliary: You've...never eaten a parfait before?
records.en: You've...never eaten a parfait before?

records.jp: パフェ、なるほどこれがパフェか。<CR>しかし上に載っているのはアイスクリームというやつだろう？
records.en_original: So this is the elusive parfait... This part on top is ice cream, correct?
records.en_auxiliary: So this is the elusive parfait... This part on top is ice cream, correct?
records.en: Parfait... So this is a parfait.<CR>But the topping is what they call ice cream, correct?

records.jp: パフェにもいろいろな種類とトッピングがあるんだよ。これは<CR>ストロベリーアイスパフェ。バナナとかチョコも載せられるけど
records.en_original: You can top a parfait with lots of different things. That's a strawberry parfait, but there's banana ones, chocolate...
records.en_auxiliary: You can top them with lots of different things. This is a strawberry parfait, but you can put stuff like banana and chocolate on them too.
records.en: There are all kinds of parfaits and toppings.<CR>This is a strawberry ice cream parfait, but you can add banana or chocolate too.

records.jp: なんということだ。<CR>かくも複雑なオペレーションを市井の店舗が実現しているとは……
records.en_original: It beggars belief that such a complex operation is underway behind the doors of a seemingly average shop...
records.en_auxiliary: It's beyond belief that such a complex operation is underway behind the doors of a seemingly average shop...
records.en: Incredible.<CR>To think an ordinary shop could carry out such a complex operation...

records.jp: まさか、これほどなんて……
records.en_original: This is ridiculous...
records.en_auxiliary: This is ridiculous...
records.en: I can't believe it was this extreme...

records.jp: ん？　どうした
records.en_original: Hm? What is?
records.en_auxiliary: Hm? What is?
records.en: Hm? What's wrong?

records.jp: いや、世間知らずだとは思ってたけど、<CR>ここまで知らないとは思わなくて
records.en_original: I mean, I knew you weren't exactly "worldly," but I didn't know how oblivious you were to everyday life.
records.en_auxiliary: I mean, I knew you weren't exactly worldly, but I didn't know how oblivious you were to everyday life.
records.en: I knew you were sheltered,<CR>but I didn't realize you knew this little about everyday life.

records.jp: 正直、私も驚いている。<CR>ここまで世間一般と私の常識がかけ離れていたとは
records.en_original: Frankly, I agree. I never expected there would be such a gap between the real world and my understanding of it.
records.en_auxiliary: Frankly, I agree. I never expected there would be such a gap between the real world and my understanding of it.
records.en: Honestly, I am surprised too.<CR>I had not realized my common sense was so far removed from everyone else's.

records.jp: 普通、本屋さんで本の内容、<CR>いきなり書き写したりしないよ？
records.en_original: Normally, when you're at the bookstore, you don't open up a book and try to copy the contents for later reference.
records.en_auxiliary: Normally, when you're at the bookstore, you don't open up a book and try to copy the contents for later reference.
records.en: Normally, you don't suddenly start copying a book's contents<CR>while you're still in the bookstore.

records.jp: ネットで、参考になった情報をブックマークするくらいの<CR>軽い気持ちだったんだ
records.en_original: Well, I assumed doing so would be something like bookmarking an article online.
records.en_auxiliary: Well, I assumed doing so would be something like bookmarking an article online.
records.en: I treated it as casually as bookmarking<CR>useful information online.

records.jp: 食品売り場で、ミネラルウォーターの蓋を開けて<CR>飲みはじめたのは？
records.en_original: You don't open up a bottle of mineral water and drink it while you're still shopping at the grocery store, either.
records.en_auxiliary: You don't open up a bottle of mineral water and drink it while you're still shopping at the grocery store, either.
records.en: And why did you open a bottle of mineral water<CR>and start drinking it in the grocery section?

records.jp: 飲食した分を後で精算するシステムなのかなと
records.en_original: I assumed they had a system where they calculated what you consumed while you were inside the store.
records.en_auxiliary: I assumed they had a system where they calculated what you consumed while you were inside the store.
records.en: I assumed it was a system where you paid afterward for whatever you consumed.

records.jp: 服屋さんでいきなり服を着替え出したのは
records.en_original: How about when you started taking off your clothes in the middle of that boutique?
records.en_auxiliary: How about when you started changing clothes in the middle of that boutique?
records.en: And why did you suddenly start changing clothes in the clothing store?

records.jp: 試着室というものがあるのを知らなかったんだ。<CR>あと、周りの人があんなに騒ぐと思わなくて……
records.en_original: I had no prior knowledge of the concept of a dressing room. ...Nor did I know how poorly the other patrons would react.
records.en_auxiliary: I had no prior knowledge of the concept of a dressing room. ...Nor did I know how poorly the other patrons would react.
records.en: I did not know dressing rooms existed.<CR>And I did not expect everyone around me to make such a commotion...

records.jp: よく今まで生活してこられたね……。<CR>子供の頃とか、親に注意されなかったの？
records.en_original: How did you manage to survive until now? Didn't your parents teach you any of this?
records.en_auxiliary: How did you manage to survive until now? Didn't your parents teach you any of this?
records.en: How have you managed to live this long...?<CR>Didn't your parents warn you when you were a child?

records.jp: 君はサヴァン症候群、という言葉を知っているか？
records.en_original: Have you ever heard of savant syndrome?
records.en_auxiliary: Have you ever heard of savant syndrome?
records.en: Have you ever heard of savant syndrome?

records.jp: え……何？　さばんな？
records.en_original: I...can't say I have. What was it again?
records.en_auxiliary: Huh? Savanna what now?
records.en: What...? Savant?

records.jp: サヴァン・シンドローム。脳の機能不全に伴う症状の一つだよ。<CR>記憶力や計算能力、状況把握能力が常人に比べて異様に高くなる
records.en_original: Savant syndrome. In which a developmentally disabled person displays above-average calculative and cognitive ability.
records.en_auxiliary: Savant syndrome. In which a developmentally challenged person displays above-average calculative and cognitive ability.
records.en: Savant syndrome. It is one symptom associated with impaired brain function.<CR>Memory, calculation, and situational awareness can become abnormally advanced compared with most people.

records.jp: まぁそもそも、現代医学ではそれらの因果関係すら<CR>解明できていないがね
records.en_original: Admittedly, the reasons for it are still unclear to modern scientists...
records.en_auxiliary: Admittedly, the reasons for it are still unclear to modern scientists...
records.en: Though modern medicine has not even clarified<CR>the causal relationship between those things.

records.jp: わかっているのは経験上、コミュニケーション障害を持つ者の<CR>極一部に、特殊な能力を発症させる者がいる、ということだ
records.en_original: But some people with communication impairments have been known to develop certain skills at an incredible rate.
records.en_auxiliary: But some people with communication impairments have been known to develop certain skills at an incredible rate.
records.en: What experience has shown is that a very small number of people with communication disorders<CR>develop exceptional abilities.

records.jp: ふぅん……。で？　その……サヴァン症候群がどうかしたの？
records.en_original: Hmm... And? Why bring that...savant syndrome up now?
records.en_auxiliary: Hmm... And? Why bring savant syndrome up now?
records.en: Hmm... And? What does that savant syndrome have to do with this?

records.jp: 私も幼い頃にその症状があると診断されてね。<CR>海外のギフテッドプログラム――特殊教育課程に進まされたんだ
records.en_original: Because I was diagnosed with it at a young age. And my family sent me to a gifted education program overseas.
records.en_auxiliary: Because I was diagnosed with it at a young age. And my family sent me to a gifted education program overseas.
records.en: I was diagnosed with it when I was young.<CR>I was sent overseas to a gifted program—a special education curriculum.

records.en_original: Oh...
records.en_auxiliary: Oh...
records.en: Oh...

records.jp: おかげで普通の学校生活を送れるくらいにはなったがね。<CR>まともな同年代の思考回路は未だによく分からないままだ
records.en_original: Thanks to that, I'm able to attend school somewhat normally. Though I'm still at a loss as to how to relate to people.
records.en_auxiliary: Thanks to that, I'm able to attend school somewhat normally. Though I'm still at a loss as to how to relate to people.
records.en: Thanks to that, I became capable of attending an ordinary school.<CR>But I still do not understand how typical people my age think.

records.jp: 皮肉だろう？　物理学や数学をいくら究めたところで<CR>一番身近なヒトの心というものが私には理解できないんだ
records.en_original: Ironic, isn't it? Despite my mastery of math and physics, people and their emotions still elude my understanding.
records.en_auxiliary: Ironic, isn't it? Despite my mastery of math and physics, people and their emotions still elude my understanding.
records.en: Ironic, is it not? No matter how deeply I master physics and mathematics,<CR>I still cannot understand something as close to me as the human heart.

records.jp: そう……だったんだ
records.en_original: I...never knew.
records.en_auxiliary: I...never knew.
records.en: I see...

records.jp: なんか、ごめん。<CR>立ち入ったこと聞いちゃって
records.en_original: I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to force that story out of you.
records.en_auxiliary: I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to force that story out of you.
records.en: Sorry.<CR>I asked something too personal.

records.jp: 構わないよ。私にとっては今更の話だ。<CR>誇ることでも卑下することでもない
records.en_original: I don't mind. It's my story. I don't feel any shame in telling it.
records.en_auxiliary: I don't mind. It's my story. I don't feel any shame in telling it.
records.en: It is fine. To me, it is a matter long past.<CR>It is neither something to take pride in nor something to belittle myself over.

records.jp: そろそろ行くか？　もう日も沈む。家の人も心配するだろう
records.en_original: Now, aren't you going to leave? The sun's about to set. You don't want to worry your family.
records.en_auxiliary: Now, shouldn't you be going? The sun's about to set. You don't want to worry your family.
records.en: Shall we go? The sun is already setting. Your family will worry.

records.jp: あ、あのさ！　有理！
records.en_original: Um...! Yuri!
records.en_auxiliary: Um! Yuri!
records.en: Um...! Yuri!

records.jp: ん？
records.en_original: Hm?
records.en_auxiliary: Hm?
records.en: Hm?

records.jp: （有理がヒトの心をわからないとか……信じられない。<CR>でもそれをどう言えば伝わるんだろう）
records.en_original: (It's hard to believe that Yuri can't understand people's emotions... But what can I say to her?)
records.en_auxiliary: (It's hard to believe that Yuri can't understand people's emotions... But what can I say to her?)
records.en: (I can't believe Yuri doesn't understand the human heart...<CR>But how can I put that into words she would understand?)

records.jp: （わからない。有理を納得させられる言葉が見つけられない）
records.en_original: (I don't know. Anything I might be able to say to her could come off as patronizing...)
records.en_auxiliary: (I don't know. Anything I say might just come off as patronizing...)
records.en: (I don't know. I can't find the words that would convince Yuri.)

records.jp: なんでもない。うん……帰ろうか。<CR>ああでも、学校まで一緒にいくよ。荷物も多くなっちゃったし
records.en_original: Oh, it's nothing. You're right, I should be going. But let's head back to school together, first.
records.en_auxiliary: It's nothing. You're right, I should be going. Oh, but let's head back to school together first.
records.en: It's nothing. Yeah...let's go.<CR>But I'll walk with you to the school. We have a lot of bags now.

records.jp: 手分けして運ぼうよ
records.en_original: That's a lot of stuff to carry alone. I'll help you out.
records.en_auxiliary: That's a lot of stuff to carry alone. I'll help you out.
records.en: Let's split the load.

records.jp: そうか、すまないな
records.en_original: You're right. I appreciate it.
records.en_auxiliary: You're right. I appreciate it.
records.en: I see. Thank you.
